main_text.p: atque his probè perpensis non amplius mirare! cùm & ubivis Terrarum quin & per mundum universum vis eadem occurrat. Sed ex superioribus, quæ tradita à nobis, hæc facilè diluuntur. Ac (ane beneficio Pulveris, sanguini vel materiæ purulentæ aspersi, aditum parari ipsi animæ mundi, substantiæ nimirum corporea mole carenti, ac quæ instar formarum substantia-lium habet, docente Papinio, ad intimiores particulas, id perinde omnino est, ac si beneficio affumptorum patefieret aditus formis animalium substantialibus, seu eorundem animabus, ad corporum penitiora, minisque ipsorum corporum particulas. Hoc unum addam: mente concipi non posse, quonam modo cœlestis illa substantia fluxilior, seu diffluxilis, ut loquitur Papinius, è sanguine effuso vel pure emigrans, atque vulnus vel ulcus unde manavit, repetens, sese sum devehere queat ad partem affe-ctam,

page.notes: Page is a running text page; the text is in a small italic-influenced roman face with some words in italic (Papinio, ubivis, Terrarum, vel). Some letters are faint or damaged; the last line is partly cut at the foot. The printed text was read with reasonable confidence but several words near the scan's ink-smudged areas (e.g. "substantia", "minisque", "sese sum") are doubtful and should be checked against the original. Italic words in the transcription are not marked with <i> because of uncertainty.
